## Summary

Built a persisted, bounded **presentation ledger** plus its test suite, entirely within the reserved paths:
- `apps/web/src/session/presentationLedger.ts` (new)
- `apps/web/test/session/presentationLedger.test.ts` (new)

### What it does
- Exports the four caps (`MAX_ACKNOWLEDGED_EVENT_IDS` 512, `MAX_PENDING_EVENTS` 64, `MAX_SEQUENCE_LAG` 300, `MAX_ROLL_CONTEXTS` 64), `RollContext`, `PresentationLedgerData`, `emptyLedgerData`, `PresentationLedgerStorage`, `PresentableEvent`, `PresentationSessionOptions`, `PresentationSession`.
- `PresentationLedgerStorage` keys on `digitable.presented.v1:${scope}`, strictly validates on `load()` (returns `null` for bad JSON/wrong types/over-cap/duplicates, tolerates unknown top-level keys), and `save()` merges with stored state (per-partition cursor max, ack-id union, rollContext union with incoming value winning and newest position) inside `try/catch`, returning `false` on any storage failure.
- `PresentationSession` ingests tail pages: ingests bookkeeping and roll contexts even for ignored/acknowledged records; merges copies by `eventId` preferring gm > member > shared and listing all partitions; orders pending by sequence then `eventId`; fires lag- and pending-cap expiry; keeps a monotonically non-decreasing per-partition cursor (pending holds it just below the minimum; otherwise it advances to the highest ingested); persists on change. No wall clock, no randomness, inputs never mutated, outputs are copies.
- Documented the FIFO-eviction safety invariant in a header comment.

### Test coverage
24 Vitest cases: storage validation/round-trip/scope isolation/merge/throw-safety; ordering, cross-partition dedupe/preference, split-page acknowledged-copy rejection, reload behavior, cursor monotonicity, FIFO ack and rollContext caps/replacement, roll-context extraction from ignored records and persistence across reload, `fetchCursor` semantics, lag/pending-cap expiry, and no-extractor mode. Plus one `fast-check` property (N ≤ 60 events, random partition subsets, schedule of split per-partition fetches, acks, reloads, then drain) asserting acknowledged/expired ids never reappear, the cursor never decreases, and the ack list stays within cap.
